facts.text: De Smet was named for the Belgian Catholic priest Pierre De Smet, a 19th-century Jesuit missionary.

Founded by Jesuit missionaries, De Smet’s mission provided religious, educational, and agricultural support, helping the Coeur d'Alene people transition to settled agrarian life after reservation boundary changes.
The Coeur d'Alene Mission of the Sacred Heart was relocated to De Smet in 1877 from Cataldo, becoming the community’s historic Jesuit mission.
Mission buildings owned by the Coeur d'Alene Tribal Council were listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975 for their religious and educational significance.
Precipitation averages about 25 inches annually, with winter months receiving over 3 inches each and summer months under 0.7 inches, reflecting a rain shadow influence.
Temperature ranges from summer highs near 90°F to winter lows below 0°F, showing continental influence despite moderating westerly winds.
